_meta.description: SEALED parameters for the Cowen cyber-cost Monte Carlo, translated from parameter_sheet.md (sealed Aug 10, 2026, Brad Carson). Units $B unless the field name says otherwise.
_meta.units: USD billions ($B) unless a field name says otherwise
_interpretation_notes: Quantile mapping: (p10/mode/p90) triples matched on p10/p90 exactly (lognormal positive, normal sign-free, beta for probabilities); mode used as consistency check only.

S1 parameterized by frequency x MEAN severity (sev_mean_usd): sheet says 'mu set to match mean', so the lognormal mu co-varies with sigma to hold the mean — mean-parameterization implements this exactly. Product of medians (10.31M x $17,450) = $180B 2024 level -> ~$260B 2026, matching the sealed S1 level prior (150/260/450 at 2026).
S1 baseline growth = fitted measured-trend growth ^ (1 - reporting_growth_share), the log-space version of sheet 'measured growth x (1 - reporting share)'.
S2 frequency grows at its own sealed trend (+3/+8/+15%/yr), not the loss-series trend; the 3x3 cell ratio still rescales the S1+S2 delta.
S2 GPD scale prior encodes the sealed median-exceedance $1.2B (0.8-2.0) at modal xi=0.95: scale = excess x xi/(2^xi - 1).

S3a payments-infrastructure = 3 tiers (Lloyd's triple used directly, not the weighted average) x first-year share (0.30/0.40/0.55): sev median = total x share-median 0.406. Tier probabilities encoded as tight Betas (published anchors).
S3a severity triples split 50/50 in log space between epistemic (sev_median prior) and aleatory (sev_sigma_log) so the TOTAL severity distribution matches the sheet triple.
S3a dependence_shift = per-regime target rho minus modal baseline rho (0.10).

S3b restructured to the sheet's 8 parameters; event rate = campaigns x P(foothold) x P(damaging); s3_prob_mult NOT applied to S3b (sheet: 'prob mult on S3a scenarios'); 2028 rate held at 2027 level (no sealed growth), subject to D-15 damping. Generative model documented in engine.py; seed_share/ref_share/max_cycles are declared structural constants [U].

Defense = per-regime severity-truncation haircut only (sheet section 4 row); the placeholder detection/patch/containment machinery is removed. Truncation is an AI shift-factor: 2028 deviation ramps at 1.5x and is subject to D-15 damping (literal reading of 'all AI multipliers').

Ch2 reporting_correction = 1/(1 + post-break uplift): section-6 header says corrections are APPLIED to measured outcomes; the correction converts apparent-basis excess to true excess (multiplier < 1, conservative).

Ch1 delta = category_deflator x [vendor_2026 x (1+labor_mult)] x ((1+g+delta_pp/100)^n - (1+g)^n), n = year-2026; sealed growth-rate-delta formulation replaces the placeholder absolute-$ prior. loss_response_coef retained as declared structural [U] (D-15 mechanism c). Ch1 delta is NOT damped by D-15 (it is not a section-4 multiplier; post-event spend rises).
Ch4 phase-in 50% weight 2027 / 100% 2028 (sheet section 7) applied in engine stats; the site export carries full-weight Ch4 samples (site has no per-year Ch4 dimension).

Ch2 loss series = IC3 x 12 (modal underreporting 5 x modal US->global 2.4), constant scale so growth equals the measured IC3 trend; 2026 quarters extrapolated at realized 2025 growth [U]. Chainalysis ransomware series is reported as honest tension, not blended into the trend.
Ch1 spend series growth-spliced across Gartner 2018/2024 series breaks, anchored 2026 = $240B; 2016->17 and the two bridge growths are [U] declared.
Quarterly values are geometric within-year interpolations of annual totals (documented; only ratios and window membership matter to the fits).
D-15 trigger compares the AI-world systemic total (S3a + S3b when both variants run) against damping_trigger_busd; damping factor drawn once per outer draw.
ILS check: Matterhorn Re attaches at $9B US industry insured loss; converted to global economic via modal econ:insured 7:1 and modal US->global 2.449 -> threshold ~$154B.
Baseline growth prior (11/12.5/14%/yr, section 5) is subsumed by the fitted 3x3 spend matrix; recorded here for the appendix.
sheet section 3a note: the old $120B infra working bound is retired to p90+ per the sheet; prior encodes p10 $8B / p90 $120B.
